newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Apart from reducing the level of fines to make collection more viable, new tax crimes legislation will be valid retroactively, giving the state the ability to reschedule outstanding debts, according to Deputy Finance Minister George Drys.

--Interest rates closed slightly higher than those set by the finance ministry during yesterday's bond auction. Despite market optimism, only three-year bonds brought returns of more than 10.0 percent.
--Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, plans to buy 49 new aircraft at a cost of one trillion drachmas, part of plans still pending approval by the government.
--The Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) is expected to ask the government for measures to support Greek businesses active in the Balkans, following the losses suffered by Greek firms in Albania.
--Tax services are bracing for major changes, including the closure of 42 tax offices and the merger of another 15 into seven, part of efforts to make tax collection more effective.

--This year's submission of the form on major real estate holdings is considered to be a litmus test of the efficiency of the measure: the finance ministry has yet to make an estimate of returns from the measure and will decide later in the year whether the 25 million drachmas forecast in the budget is a realistic target.
--The Capital Market Commission has imposed fines of up to 10 million drachmas on 22 listed firms because of their failure to adhere to rules on publishing their half-yearly accounts.

--SEB has welcomed statements by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou on state and private cooperation in the Balkans but has also requested that the government seriously consider compensation for those suffering losses in Albania.
--The anxiety over the course of tax revenues continues to preoccupy the government's economic team, despite a slight improvement in the first two weeks of March.

--Yesterday's bond auction sent a clear message that the time is not yet ripe for a further fall in interest rates. Sources say the finance ministry has "got the message" and will hold off on further interest rate cuts for the next few months.
--Dozens of hoteliers are displeased with very short notice over rescheduling of debts to the Hellenic Industrial and Development Bank.
--A European Commission official said yesterday that Greece's absorption of Cohesion Fund allocations was not facing any problems this year. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
